overall: The AG found two violations: the March 11, 2014 notice omitted the employee whose contract was discussed, and the May 27, 2014 notice omitted the Entero project; all other allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly lacked a proper statutory purpose for the March 11, 2014 executive session on contract negotiations with an employee.
allegations.key_passage: This fit squarely within the ambit of Purpose 2.

allegations.summary: March 11, 2014 notice did not identify the employee (wiring inspector) whose contract would be discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, it should have been included on the notice, and its omission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: May 27, 2014 notice omitted the Entero project, which was discussed in executive session alongside listed projects.
allegations.key_passage: The Board has not identified any reason why the Entero project could not be listed on the meeting notice. We therefore find that its omission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Executive session discussion of consolidating Town departments was not raised in the complaint; the AG noted it was more appropriate for open session.
allegations.key_passage: We have concluded in the past that such wide-ranging financial discussions are akin to budget discussions, and must therefore take place in open session.

allegations.summary: June 5, 2014 executive session minutes were allegedly inaccurate, repeating May 27 minutes, though no executive session was held that day.
January 20, 2015 notice allegedly failed to list a discussion of Route 44 property and urban renewal.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board reasonably believed that disclosing identifying information about the urban renewal plan or the properties at issue would compromise the Town's negotiating position, we conclude that the Board was justified in omitting identifying information from the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: January 20, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly lacked detail on the police contract discussion, including funding sources.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the January 20, 2015 executive session minutes accurately summarize the discussion that took place.

allegations.summary: May 19, 2015 notice allegedly did not describe the real estate matters under discussion in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Board reasonably believed that disclosing it would have compromised the town's negotiating position.

allegations.summary: May 19, 2015 minutes allegedly lacked enough information about the Eversource project discussed.
allegations.key_passage: While additional information about the project may have been helpful to members of the public, we find that the minutes accurately summarize the brief discussion that took place.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly should not have redacted portions of the May 2015 executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Based on our conversation with the Board's legal counsel, we credit this statement and we find that the Board permissibly withheld portions of the executive session minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: Wc order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
